draft.title: Angle sum of polygons
card: A polygon is a closed shape with straight sides. Pick one vertex (corner) and draw lines to every other vertex that is not next to it. This splits the polygon into triangles.
Each triangle has an angle sum of 180°. A quadrilateral splits into 2 triangles, so its angles add to 2 × 180° = 360°.
A polygon with n sides splits into n − 2 triangles. Its angles add to (n − 2) × 180°.
draft.remember: Number of triangles = n − 2, so the angle sum is (n − 2) × 180°.

a.q: What is the angle sum of a pentagon, which has 5 sides?
a.why: A pentagon splits into 5 − 2 = 3 triangles, so the sum is 3 × 180° = 540°. 720° would be the sum for a hexagon, which has 6 sides.
a.clue: Find n − 2 first, then multiply by 180°.

b.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 95°, 110° and 70°. What is the fourth angle?
b.why: The four angles add to 360°. 95° + 110° + 70° = 275°, and 360° − 275° = 85°. 275° is the sum of the three known angles, not the missing one.
b.clue: Subtract the three known angles from the quadrilateral's total.
